findings.title: A measured warrant for redress
findings.claim: The focus grants the slain person's wali a real claim to remedy wrongful killing, while its immediate prohibition of excess keeps that remedy within a publicly stated measure. Wider passages let the wali's sultan carry authority and proof readings together, with the protected life and the possibility of pardon remaining in view.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are the life made inviolable, the bi-l-haqq exception, the wronged victim, li-waliyyihi sultanan, and fa-la yusrif fi al-qatl. The repeated protected-life clause in 25:68 and 6:151 keeps inviolability present through the remedy. Qisas, family compensation, remission, and equal response in 2:178, 4:92, 5:45, and 2:194 connect the wali's grant to an identifiable claim and limit. Equivalence and pardon in 16:126 and 42:40, together with the wrong-without-right boundary in 42:42, make excess a failure of measure. In 27:21, punishment or slaughter is conditioned on bringing a clear sultan; 7:33 rejects a sultan not revealed by God. Those contexts return through the focus's sultan and its right-condition, so the grant reads as both force-capable authority and a warrant held to measure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the authority can answer a serious wrong without turning the remedy into another wrong. The repeated protection of life, the defined claim-holder, and the equivalent-response pattern explain one another; pardon remains beside requital.
findings.containment: The focus does not define every case covered by al-haqq, specify a court or modern legal procedure, or resolve whether its final pronoun refers to the wali or the slain person. The connection targets have exact Arabic but no supplied target morphology, and 27:21 is an analogy from a different scene rather than the same legal rule.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication supplies exact focus anchors and the focus morphology is aligned. Wider target Arabic is supplied, but its morphology is not; the coercive and proof facets of sultan remain contextual readings, so the cross-ayah claim is qualified.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: çiğnenmemesi gereken saygınlık ve korunmuş hak
branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişinin saygınlığı ve hakkı, başkalarına onu incitmeme ve hakkını zedelememe yükümlülüğü getirir.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 25:68 and 6:151 repeat the protected-nafs clause; 2:194 places inviolable claims in an equivalent-response frame.
branch_activations.activation: The repeated prohibition meets the focus's sanctification of the life, while the wider equal-response wording keeps the protected status present when redress is permitted.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The remedy answers a violation of a protected right without making that right expire.
branch_activations.boundary: This is the protected-social-right facet, not a protected-place reading or a complete definition of every prohibition; the wider verses have their own settings.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 25:68 and 6:151 repeat the nafs clause; 5:32 compares killing one nafs with killing all people and reviving one with reviving them all.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The protected unit is a living person whose loss carries significance beyond an isolated case.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not reduce nafs to a biological definition or equate the distinct settings of the connected passages.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The exception can be heard as an entitlement with a claimant and measure, alongside its general right-condition.
branch_activations.boundary: The connected passages have distinct legal contexts; they do not specify identical beneficiaries or settle every application of haqq.

findings.title: Support reaches the wronged
findings.claim: The focus's closing passive support can carry the result of redress for the wronged person as well as aid to the wali entrusted with the claim. Wider passages join being wronged with help and bring the slain person into a public question about the killing.
findings.mechanism: The focus first names a person killed maẓlūman, assigns a sultan to the wali, and closes with an open singular referent and the passive manṣūran. In 22:39, being wronged grounds permission and God's ability to aid is named; in 4:75, the oppressed ask for both a wali and a helper; 42:41 leaves redress after wrong without blame. In 81:8-9, the buried girl is asked for what sin she was killed. These contacts return through the focus's wronged person, wali, killing, and passive support, allowing the final aid to include the victim's vindication alongside support for the representative.
findings.reader_payoff: The slain person remains in view after the wali receives authority: the remedy answers a particular wrong, and the wider frame also places the victim's killing before a question.
findings.containment: This does not resolve the referent of innahu, identify an institution that provides support, or establish a postmortem or judicial procedure. The cited connection targets supply exact Arabic but not target morphology, so the cross-ayah relations remain contextual.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk support is legacy_unbound and non-citable, so it only nominates the closing support dimension. The focus surface and exact Arabic in the supplied connections ground a narrower contextual reading; target morphology is absent and the pronoun remains open.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Mağdurun haksızlık yapan kişiden hakkını veya yapılan kötülüğün karşılığını almasıdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus presents the wronged slain person, assigns the claim to a wali, and ends with the passive state manṣūran.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 42:41 names redress after a person's wrong and leaves no blame against those who seek it.
branch_activations.activation: The active redress-after-wrong relation meets the focus's delegated wali and passive support result; the redress branch can enter through the wali's act while the slain person remains its beneficiary.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The closing support can carry vindication as the outcome of redress, without making the slain person the active retaliator.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus is passive and leaves the final pronoun open; this does not identify the support's agent or authorize excess.

branch_activations.activation: The wider aid-to-oppressed relation meets the focus's wronged person and passive support clause, extending the closing support to the victim's side of the remedy.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Aid can be heard as reaching the slain person's vindication as well as the wali's entrusted work.
branch_activations.boundary: Target morphology is not supplied; this is a contextual resonance from the exact Arabic, not a new analysis of those target words.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 81:8-9 brings the buried girl into question and asks for what sin she was killed.
branch_activations.activation: The wider questioning of a slain victim meets the focus's passive killing and wronged-person carriers, making the victim's own case visible alongside the wali's claim.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The wrongfully slain person remains a subject of accountability, not only the object of a representative's authority.
branch_activations.boundary: The connection concerns a distinct victim and setting; it does not settle the focus's pronoun or specify the form of accountability.
